text: Rocket fuel 4/10 — tank pressures within limits.
Rocket fuel 6/10 — fill rates holding steady.
Launch Control: Beginning terminal system checks.
Flight: All stations, stand by for launch.
Crew: Loud and clear, Launch Control.
Crew: Visors down, pressure seals checked.
Ground: Access arm ready for retraction.
Launch Control: All personnel clear the pad.
Flight: Coming up on final Go/No-Go poll.
Flight: We are Go for launch.
Flight: Final status check: all stations Go.
Launch Control: T-minus 18 seconds and counting.
Flight: Vehicle has cleared the launch complex.
Guidance: Pitch and roll program initiated.
Flight: Passing through low cloud layer.
Flight: Standing by for staging sequence.
Crew: A brief jolt, all good.
Guidance: Orbit insertion parameters looking good.
Flight: All flight controllers, monitor insertion.
Flight: Stand by for orbital confirmation.
Crew: Earth looks magnificent from up here.
Flight: You are Go for attitude adjustment.
Crew: Requesting permission for the first space snack.
Flight: Permission granted. Mind the crumbs.
Crew: The window view is better than advertised.
Crew: Earth is shrinking behind us.
Navigation: Star tracker has acquired reference stars.
Crew: Everything outside is exceptionally quiet.
Crew: Our coffee is conducting independent orbital operations.
Flight: Maintain heading. Next checkpoint ahead.
Sensors: Unidentified faint signal on the forward array.
Mission Control: Entering unexplored mission phase.
Navigation: The star chart no longer matches the view.
Crew: Those lights just changed formation.
Sensors: Objects appear to be matching our velocity.
Communications: Receiving a signal with no known origin.
Computer: Signal resembles a greeting. Probability uncertain.
Communications: Response received before transmission finished.
Navigation: Local geometry is behaving strangely.
Crew: There is a perfectly black rectangle ahead.
Computer: Object dimensions are suspiciously exact.
Crew: Does anyone else hear a choir?
Computer: No audio source detected. Also, I am not singing.
Flight: Keep a safe distance from the object.
Sensors: Object vanished without measurable acceleration.
Navigation: New course available. Destination unknown.
Computer: Democracy acknowledged. Risk assessment pending.
Sensors: A planet has appeared where none was catalogued.
Navigation: Planet has two suns. That complicates sunrise.
Crew: We have a distinctly bad feeling about this.
Sensors: Large artificial structure near the outer moon.
Flight: Please avoid the artificial moon.
Computer: Artificial moon avoidance route calculated.
Communications: Receiving coordinates and a dinner invitation.
Crew: Ask whether spacesuits are required for dinner.
Communications: Reply says: 'Only if you insist.'
Navigation: Entering orbit around the unknown planet.
Sensors: Atmosphere contains oxygen and several unpronounceable gases.
Crew: We can see cities glowing on the night side.
Computer: Message translated: 'Please use visitor parking.'
Navigation: A docking corridor has illuminated itself.
Flight: Proceed at minimum relative velocity.
Crew: The airlock is larger on the inside.
Computer: Internal volume exceeds external volume. Noted.
Crew: A floating jellyfish is waving at us.
Crew: They appear friendly and extremely curious about duct tape.
Computer: Their technology runs entirely on improbable confidence.
Crew: Exchanging maps. Theirs has four more dimensions.
Mission Control: First contact officially recorded.
Alien Control: Permission granted to depart via Gate Seven.
Navigation: Gate Seven is a ring suspended in empty space.
Crew: Setting course for the ring.
Computer: Hyperspace mathematics appear mostly decorative.
Alien Control: Please keep hands inside the universe.
Flight: All stations, secure for transit.
Crew: The stars are bending into lines.
Computer: Current position cannot be represented with three coordinates.
Crew: We just passed ourselves going the other direction.
Navigation: Transit complete. Unknown galaxy confirmed.
Sensors: A vast fleet is arranged around a luminous cloud.
Crew: Every ship seems to be playing a different song.
Computer: The fleet identifies as a traveling orchestra.
Communications: Invitation to the Galactic Welcome Festival.
Mission Control: Permission granted. Stay on schedule, somehow.
Sensors: A small comet is following us like a pet.
Crew: We have named the comet Kevin.
Navigation: New coordinates received from the festival fleet.
Crew: Setting course for home, plus or minus one galaxy.
Computer: Earth location reacquired. Timeline uncertain.
Crew: Is it still Tuesday on Earth?
Navigation: Final approach to familiar space.
Sensors: Earth detected. One moon. Comforting.
Flight: Mission Control has your signal again.
Crew: We brought souvenirs and several questions.
Mission Control: Prepare for mission completion.
Mission complete. Welcome home, cosmic explorer!
